name: Tinder bundle and fire lay
summary: The structure that turns an ember or a spark into a fire — a bird's nest of fine dry fibre inside a graded stack of fuel.
time: 20-30 minutes of gathering before you strike anything

steps.text: Gather everything BEFORE you light anything: three graded piles — hair-fine tinder, pencil-thick kindling, thumb-thick and up. Gather twice what you think you need.
steps.why: The commonest way a fire dies is running out of the next size up while the flame is still fragile.

steps.text: Take dead wood from standing trees, not from the ground. Snap it: it should crack, not bend.
Work the tinder between your palms until it is a mass of loose fibre, then shape it into a nest with a hollow in the middle.
Build the lay on a dry base — a bark slab or flat stone — so the ground does not wick heat and damp out of it.
Drop the ember into the nest, fold it loosely closed, hold it up and breathe long and steady through it until it flames.
Set the flaming nest under the kindling and feed it upward in size, never smothering the flame with a piece it cannot catch.

verify: Tinder is ready when it is fibre, not shavings — it should look like a bird's nest and light from a single spark.
The fire is established when thumb-thick wood burns without your attention.
limits: A perfect ignition source cannot rescue bad tinder or a wet lay. Preparation is the part that actually determines whether you get fire.
This is the structure only — it presumes a separate ignition source (`fire-bow-drill`, `fire-ferro-rod`, a lighter).
cautions: Clear the ground to bare earth and mind overhanging branches and roots — a fire can travel underground through duff and root mats.
Never build a fire under a snow-loaded branch.
